Day One

KITCHEN NOTES / DAY ONE

How to hold a knife and not get hurt

Do not hold the food with flat fingers. Learn the claw grip so the knife rests against your knuckles, not your fingertips.

Pinch → Claw → Slice
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Pinch the blade

    Do not grip the handle like a baseball bat. Pinch the base of the blade with your thumb and index finger.

    Look for You have much more control over the tip of the knife this way.

  2. 02

    Make a claw

    Tuck the fingertips of your other hand inward, like a bear claw. Rest your knuckles against the side of the blade.

    Look for Your fingertips are completely hidden and safe.

  3. 03

    Slice, do not chop

    Move the knife in a forward and downward circle, like a locomotive wheel. Do not aggressively hack straight down.

    Look for The sharp edge slices smoothly without needing a lot of force.

  4. 04

    Stabilize the board

    Put a damp paper towel under your cutting board so it does not slide around.

    Look for The board should feel cemented to the counter.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

The side of the blade gently glides against your knuckles as you slice.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Laying your fingers flat on the food while cutting.

A knife resting against flat fingers is an accident waiting to happen.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Tuck your fingertips away into the claw grip.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

If you are cutting something round like an onion, slice it in half first so it lays flat and stable on the board.

Knife feels dull?

A dull knife is more dangerous than a sharp one because you have to push harder, increasing the chance of slipping.
